parts.text:
I'm building a wiki for the repository at /tmp/openwiki-bench-pS6clC (a Cloudflare Workers-based "Gadgets Workshop" platform). I need a thorough understanding of the frontend SPA. Be "very thorough".

Read and summarize packages/workshop-frontend/src:
1. main.tsx, router.tsx, routeTree.gen.ts, routes/ (routing structure / pages)
2. RpcContext.tsx, App.tsx, AuthContext.tsx, ServerConfigContext.tsx
3. ChatInterface.tsx (the main chat UI) and its supporting hooks
4. GadgetUI.tsx, GadgetEditor.tsx, GadgetCodeInterface.tsx, CodeEditor.tsx, CodeDiffEditor.tsx
5. Connections.tsx, AdminPage.tsx, SettingsPage.tsx, LoginPage.tsx, SignupPage.tsx, BlueprintsPage.tsx, OnboardingWizard.tsx, ShareModal.tsx
6. GatekeeperAppPage.tsx, SandboxedGatekeeperApp.tsx (how gatekeeper UIs are embedded)
7. useAuth.ts, useActions.ts, useActionHistory.ts, useAutoApproval.ts, useAlwaysApproveTag.ts, useResolveAction.ts
8. otClient.ts (operational transform), accountsSubscriber.ts (subscriptions to account data)
9. errorReporting.ts, FrontendErrorBoundary.tsx
10. data/ and utils/ directories
11. How the frontend uses Cap'n Web RPC (state stubs, disposal patterns, pipelining)
12. Themed UI system (Kumo UI)

Report back a structured summary of the SPA architecture, the main user-facing surfaces, and the RPC/data flow patterns Ring. Include concrete file paths and line numbers for key claims.
I'll thoroughly explore the frontend SPA structure. Let me start by getting an overview of the directory structure and then dive into each component.

75:       session.hasLoadedPage = true

153:   #appliedRevision = 0
154: 
155:   // ---- local (unacknowledged) state ----
156:   // At most one submission in flight (the seq rule makes that a checked invariant server-side),
157:   // plus the composition of local edits made since it left. `pending` applies on top of
158:   // `inflight.change`, which applies on top of #applied. `wire` is the payload as first sent --
159:   // retries must resend it byte-identically for the server's dedupe digest -- while `change` is the
160:   // same change as transformed over remote rows since, for local display and rebasing. `accepted`
161:   // is where the server's RPC response said the submission landed: normally the echo row
162:   // (broadcast before the response) has already cleared the whole record by the time it is
163:   // set, so it only matters as the lost-echo backstop (see #tryApplyInflightAck).
164:   #inflight: {
165:     wire: CodeChangeSubmission
166:     change: CodeChange
167:     accepted?: { generation: number; revision: number }
168:   } | null = null
169:   #pending: CodeChange = EMPTY_CHANGE
170:   // Local seeds for gadgets this client started editing before any pin existed: the head tree
171:   // the first keystroke was made against. Declared as the pin base on the next submission and
172:   // dropped once the gadget's content enters #applied (or on any rebuild/reset).
173:   #localSeeds = new Map<WorkpieceId, { baseCommit: string; files: ReadonlyMap<string, string> }>()
174: 
175:   // ---- derived ----
176:   // #applied + local seeds + inflight + pending: what editors display. Kept incrementally so
177:   // remote rows can be delivered to editors as deltas.
178:   #display: CodeContent = new Map()
179: 
180:   // ---- stream bookkeeping ----
181:   #clientId = crypto.randomUUID()
182:   #seq = 0
183:   #latestDurable: ChatDurableCode = { rowsThrough: 0 }
184:   // Rows not yet applied: held when they run ahead of the state we can apply them to (a future
185:   // generation before its metadata, a revision gap, a pin we haven't learned yet).
186:   #heldRows = new Map<number, Map<number, ChatChangeRow>>()
187:   // Set while waiting out a content-preserving generation switch (see setDurableState).
188:   #pendingSwitch: { codeBase: ChatCodeBase; since: number } | null = null
189:   // Set while the durable watermark has run ahead of the applied revision (see #checkStalls).
190:   #watermarkGapSince: number | null = null
191:   #recheckTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null
192:   // Chat-created (pending) gadgets have no head commit and build content up from nothing; rows
193:   // touching them apply against an empty base rather than waiting for a pin.
194:   #pendingCreations: ReadonlySet<WorkpieceId> = new Set()
195: 
196:   // ---- lifecycle ----
197:   #ready = false
198:   #disposed = false
199:   #fatal = false
200:   // Serializes the async work (rebuilds, row application with base fetches) so state mutations
201:   // happen in synchronous tails, in order -- mirroring the server's prefetch-then-commit
202:   // pattern. Local edits are deliberately *not* queued: they are synchronous, and the queued
203:   // tasks' synchronous tails read the then-current buffers.
204:   #queue: Promise<void> = Promise.resolve()
205:   #submitScheduled = false
206:   #submitBackoffMs = SUBMIT_RETRY_BASE_MS
207: 
208:   constructor(delegate: ChatOtClientDelegate) {
209:     this.#delegate = delegate
210:   }
211: 
212:   dispose(): void {
213:     this.#disposed = true
214:     if (this.#recheckTimer !== null) {
215:       clearTimeout(this.#recheckTimer)
216:       this.#recheckTimer = null
217:     }
218:   }

220:   /** False until the first durable snapshot has been folded (and after a fatal error). */
221:   isReady(): boolean {
222:     return this.#ready && !this.#fatal
223:   }

225:   /** The chat's uncommitted content as displayed: server-acked rows plus local edits. */
226:   getContent(): CodeContent {
227:     return this.#display
228:   }

230:   /** Whether the chat's uncommitted content covers this gadget (else it tracks head live). */
231:   hasGadget(gadgetId: WorkpieceId): boolean {
232:     return this.#display.has(gadgetId)
233:   }
234: 
235:   getFiles(gadgetId: WorkpieceId): ReadonlyMap<string, string> | undefined {
236:     return this.#display.get(gadgetId)
237:   }

239:   /** Whether unacknowledged local edits exist (in flight or still pending). */
240:   hasLocalEdits(): boolean {
241:     return this.#inflight !== null || !isEmptyChange(this.#pending)
242:   }
243: 
244:   /** Update the set of gadgets still pending (chat-created) in this chat. */
245:   setPendingCreations(ids: ReadonlySet<WorkpieceId>): void {
246:     this.#pendingCreations = ids
247:     // A held row or a waiting submission may have been waiting for exactly this knowledge.
248:     this.#enqueue(() => this.#drainHeldRows())
249:     this.#scheduleSubmit()
250:   }

252:   // =====================================================================================
253:   // Durable state / rows in
254: 
255:   /**
256:    * Fold a fresh durable snapshot (metadata + message log). Called on every recomputation;
257:    * internally decides whether it means a rebuild, a generation handoff, or nothing.
258:    */
259:   setDurableState(durable: ChatDurableCode): void {
260:     this.#enqueue(async () => {
261:       const codeBase = durable.codeBase ?? { pins: [], generation: 0, revision: 0 }
262:       // Messages can arrive before the metadata that covers their materialization watermark.
263:       if (durable.rowsThrough > codeBase.revision) return
264:       this.#latestDurable = durable
265: 
266:       if (!this.#ready) {
267:         await this.#rebuild(durable)
268:         return
269:       }
270: 
271:       if (codeBase.generation !== this.#generation) {
272:         if (codeBase.generation < this.#generation) return  // stale delivery
273:         if (codeBase.prior?.generation === this.#generation) {
274:           // Content-preserving epoch reset: finish the closed generation's tail, then hand the
275:           // local buffers across (see #trySwitchGeneration, called from the drain).
276:           this.#pendingSwitch ??= { codeBase, since: Date.now() }
277:           this.#pendingSwitch.codeBase = codeBase
278:           await this.#drainHeldRows()
279:           this.#checkStalls()
280:         } else {
281:           // Destructive bump (or a boundary we can't bridge): local edits are rooted in erased
282:           // history and must be discarded.
283:           await this.#discardLocalAndRebuild()
284:         }
285:         return
286:       }
287: 
288:       // Same generation. New pins may unblock held rows or a waiting submission; and a
289:       // watermark running ahead of the applied revision means rows are missing (usually just
290:       // still in flight through the UI layer -- see #checkStalls).
291:       await this.#drainHeldRows()
292:       this.#checkStalls()
293:       this.#scheduleSubmit()
294:     })
295:   }
296: 
297:   // Whether the durable materialization watermark has run ahead of the applied revision: rows
298:   // it covers never reached us (or haven't yet).
299:   #hasWatermarkGap(): boolean {
300:     return this.#latestDurable.rowsThrough > this.#appliedRevision &&
301:         (this.#latestDurable.codeBase?.generation ?? 0) === this.#generation &&
302:         this.#pendingSwitch === null
303:   }
304: 
305:   // Whether a rebuild would lose anything: pending edits, local seeds, or an in-flight
306:   // submission not yet known to be durably recorded. An in-flight the server has accepted at a
307:   // position the durable watermark already covers (or in a generation it has moved past) is
308:   // inside the snapshot's epochChange -- or erased with its generation -- so rebuilding from the
309:   // snapshot reproduces the server's truth without losing keystrokes.
310:   #hasUnsyncedLocalState(): boolean {
311:     if (!isEmptyChange(this.#pending) || this.#localSeeds.size > 0) return true
312:     if (this.#inflight === null) return false
313:     const accepted = this.#inflight.accepted
314:     if (accepted === undefined) return true
315:     const durableGeneration = this.#latestDurable.codeBase?.generation ?? 0
316:     return !(durableGeneration > accepted.generation ||
317:         (durableGeneration === accepted.generation &&
318:          this.#latestDurable.rowsThrough >= accepted.revision))
319:   }
320: 
321:   // Evaluate the two stall conditions (an unfinished generation handoff, a materialization
322:   // watermark ahead of the applied revision): normally they resolve within the next event
323:   // batch, so give them a grace period on a timer before concluding that events were lost and
324:   // rebuilding.
325:   #checkStalls(): void {
326:     if (this.#fatal || this.#disposed || !this.#ready) return
327:     if (this.#hasWatermarkGap()) {
328:       if (!this.#hasUnsyncedLocalState()) {
329:         // The missing rows are already inside the snapshot's epochChange and nothing local is at
330:         // risk: rebuild right away instead of stalling the view for the grace period.
331:         this.#watermarkGapSince = null
332:         this.#enqueue(async () => {
333:           if (this.#ready && this.#hasWatermarkGap() && !this.#hasUnsyncedLocalState()) {
334:             await this.#rebuild(this.#latestDurable)
335:           }
336:         })
337:         return
338:       }
339:       this.#watermarkGapSince ??= Date.now()
340:     } else {
341:       this.#watermarkGapSince = null
342:     }
343: 
344:     const stalledSince = this.#pendingSwitch?.since ?? this.#watermarkGapSince
345:     if (stalledSince === null || stalledSince === undefined) return
346:     const overdue = Date.now() - stalledSince - STALL_TIMEOUT_MS
347:     if (overdue >= 0) {
348:       this.#enqueue(() => this.#discardLocalAndRebuild())
349:       return
350:     }
351:     if (this.#recheckTimer === null) {
352:       this.#recheckTimer = setTimeout(() => {
353:         this.#recheckTimer = null
354:         this.#enqueue(async () => {
355:           await this.#drainHeldRows()
356:           this.#checkStalls()
357:         })
358:       }, -overdue + 50)
359:     }
360:   }
361: 
362:   /** Feed one changeApplied row. Duplicates (subscribe-replay) are ignored. */
363:   pushRow(row: ChatChangeRow): void {
364:     this.#enqueue(async () => {
365:       let generationRows = this.#heldRows.get(row.generation)
366:       if (!generationRows) {
367:         generationRows = new Map()
368:         this.#heldRows.set(row.generation, generationRows)
369:       }
370:       if (!generationRows.has(row.revision)) generationRows.set(row.revision, row)
371:       await this.#drainHeldRows()
372:     })
373:   }
374: 
375:   // Apply every held row that is applicable now, in revision order; stop at the first that
376:   // isn't (a gap, a future generation, or an unknown pin still awaiting metadata).
377:   async #drainHeldRows(): Promise<void> {
378:     if (!this.#ready || this.#fatal) return
379:     for (;;) {
380:       // Prune: generations fully left behind, and *applied* rows once a materialization
381:       // watermark covers them. Applied-but-unmaterialized rows are deliberately retained --
382:       // they are the local replay cache a rebuild draws on (a rebuild starts from the
383:       // messages' watermark, before rows the server still considers live). Unapplied rows are
384:       // retained even below the watermark: a row arriving just after the watermark that
385:       // absorbed it is still the stream's next step (its content and the epochChange's agree), and
386:       // dropping it would wedge the stream at the gap.
387:       for (const generation of this.#heldRows.keys()) {
388:         if (generation < this.#generation) this.#heldRows.delete(generation)
389:       }
390:       const durableBase = this.#latestDurable.codeBase
391:       const generationRows = this.#heldRows.get(this.#generation)
392:       if (generationRows && (durableBase?.generation ?? 0) === this.#generation) {
393:         const coveredThrough =
394:           Math.min(this.#latestDurable.rowsThrough, this.#appliedRevision)
395:         for (const revision of generationRows.keys()) {
396:           if (revision <= coveredThrough) generationRows.delete(revision)
397:         }
398:       }
399: 
400:       const next = generationRows?.get(this.#appliedRevision + 1)
401:       if (next !== undefined) {
402:         if (!(await this.#applyRow(next))) return
403:         continue
404:       }
405:       if (this.#tryApplyInflightAck()) continue
406:       const outcome = this.#trySwitchGeneration()
407:       if (outcome === "discard") {
408:         await this.#discardLocalAndRebuild()
409:         return
410:       }
411:       if (outcome === "idle") return
412:     }
413:   }
414: 
415:   // Apply one row (the next in sequence). Returns false if it must wait (a pin the metadata
416:   // hasn't delivered yet) or if the client's local edits had to be discarded instead.
417:   async #applyRow(row: ChatChangeRow): Promise<boolean> {
418:     // Establish bases for gadgets the row touches that content doesn't cover yet. The pin is
419:     // read from the latest metadata; the metadata carrying it is written in the same
420:     // synchronous server step as the row, so normally it has already arrived.
421:     const seeds = new Map<WorkpieceId, ReadonlyMap<string, string>>()
422:     for (const gadgetId of changedGadgets(row.change)) {
423:       if (this.#applied.has(gadgetId) || seeds.has(gadgetId)) continue
424:       const pin = (this.#latestDurable.codeBase?.pins ?? []).find(p => p.gadgetId === gadgetId)
425:       if (pin !== undefined) {
426:         const localSeed = this.#localSeeds.get(gadgetId)
427:         if (localSeed !== undefined && localSeed.baseCommit !== pin.baseCommit) {
428:           // Another client's first edit pinned this gadget at a different base than our own
429:           // not-yet-submitted first edit assumed: our declaration would be rejected as a pin
430:           // conflict, and our display no longer matches the chat. Discard and rebuild.
431:           await this.#discardLocalAndRebuild()
432:           return false
433:         }
434:         // The fetch awaits; the synchronous tail below revalidates the stream position.
435:         seeds.set(gadgetId, await this.#delegate.fetchCommitFiles(pin.baseCommit))
436:       } else if (this.#localSeeds.has(gadgetId)) {
437:         // Our own declaration's echo can arrive before the metadata that mirrors the pin; the
438:         // local seed is byte-identical to the declared base by construction.
439:         seeds.set(gadgetId, this.#localSeeds.get(gadgetId)!.files)
440:       } else if (!this.#pendingCreations.has(gadgetId)) {
441:         // No pin known yet: hold until the metadata that declares it arrives
442:         // (setDurableState / setPendingCreations re-drain).
443:         return false
444:       }
445:     }
446: 
447:     // ---- synchronous tail ----
448:     if (this.#fatal || this.#disposed) return false
449:     if (row.generation !== this.#generation || row.revision !== this.#appliedRevision + 1) {
450:       return true  // state moved during the fetch; the drain loop re-evaluates
451:     }
452: 
453:     const events: RemoteFileEvent[] = []
454:     if (seeds.size > 0) {
455:       const applied = new Map(this.#applied)
456:       const display = new Map(this.#display)
457:       for (const [gadgetId, files] of seeds) {
458:         applied.set(gadgetId, new Map(files))
459:         if (!display.has(gadgetId)) {
460:           // A newly-visible remote pin: surface its base files so an open editor re-reads.
461:           // (When we held a matching local seed, the display already shows this content.)
462:           for (const [path, text] of files) events.push({ gadgetId, path, change: { set: text } })
463:           display.set(gadgetId, new Map(files))
464:         }
465:         this.#localSeeds.delete(gadgetId)
466:       }
467:       this.#applied = applied
468:       this.#display = display
469:     }
470: 
471:     const own = row.submission !== undefined && row.submission.clientId === this.#clientId &&
472:       this.#inflight !== null && row.submission.seq === this.#inflight.wire.seq
473:     this.#applied = applyCodeChange(this.#applied, row.change)
474:     this.#appliedRevision = row.revision
475: 
476:     if (own) {
477:       // Our own echo: the broadcast change is our in-flight change as the server transformed it
478:       // -- the same transforms we applied locally -- so the display already reflects it and
479:       // editors are notified only of the seed events above (usually none). An empty call would
480:       // read as a coarse reset (see ChatOtClientDelegate.onRemoteChange).
481:       this.#inflight = null
482:       this.#submitBackoffMs = SUBMIT_RETRY_BASE_MS
483:       this.#delegate.onDirtyState(false)
484:       this.#scheduleSubmit()
485:       if (events.length > 0) this.#delegate.onRemoteChange(events)
486:       return true
487:     }
488: 
489:     // A remote row: rebase the local buffers over it (the row has priority -- the server
490:     // ordered it first) and apply its doubly-transformed form to the display.
491:     let displayChange = row.change
492:     if (this.#inflight !== null) {
493:       const { a, b } = transformCodeChange(displayChange, this.#inflight.change)
494:       displayChange = a
495:       this.#inflight.change = b
496:     }
497:     if (!isEmptyChange(this.#pending)) {
498:       const { a, b } = transformCodeChange(displayChange, this.#pending)
499:       displayChange = a
500:       this.#pending = b
501:     }
502:     this.#display = applyCodeChange(this.#display, displayChange)
503:     for (const [gadgetKey, entries] of Object.entries(displayChange)) {
504:       for (const [path, change] of entries) {
505:         events.push({ gadgetId: Number(gadgetKey), path, change })
506:       }
507:     }
508:     // A row whose doubly-transformed form changed no displayed file (and surfaced no seeds)
509:     // is a display no-op: deliver nothing rather than a spurious coarse reset.
510:     if (events.length > 0) this.#delegate.onRemoteChange(events)
511:     return true
512:   }
513: 
514:   // Backstop for a lost echo: the submission was accepted (the RPC response said where it
515:   // landed -- see #sendInflight) but its broadcast row never reached us, e.g. it was
516:   // materialized while we were disconnected so subscribe-replay no longer carries it. Once the
517:   // stream reaches the position just below the accepted one, apply our own change exactly as the
518:   // echo would have: the broadcast change is our in-flight change as the server transformed it
519:   // -- the same transforms we applied locally (see #applyRow's own-echo path).
520:   #tryApplyInflightAck(): boolean {
521:     const accepted = this.#inflight?.accepted
522:     if (accepted === undefined || accepted.generation !== this.#generation ||
523:         accepted.revision !== this.#appliedRevision + 1) {
524:       return false
525:     }
526:     const inflight = this.#inflight!
527: 
528:     // Seed gadgets our own submission's pin declarations covered (mirrors the local-seed echo
529:     // path in #applyRow); the display already shows this content.
530:     const seedGadgets = changedGadgets(inflight.change)
531:       .filter(gadgetId => !this.#applied.has(gadgetId) && this.#localSeeds.has(gadgetId))
532:     if (seedGadgets.length > 0) {
533:       const applied = new Map(this.#applied)
534:       for (const gadgetId of seedGadgets) {
535:         applied.set(gadgetId, new Map(this.#localSeeds.get(gadgetId)!.files))
536:         this.#localSeeds.delete(gadgetId)
537:       }
538:       this.#applied = applied
539:     }
540: 
541:     this.#applied = applyCodeChange(this.#applied, inflight.change)
542:     this.#appliedRevision = accepted.revision
543:     this.#inflight = null
544:     this.#submitBackoffMs = SUBMIT_RETRY_BASE_MS
545:     this.#delegate.onDirtyState(false)
546:     this.#scheduleSubmit()
547:     return true
548:   }
549: 
550:   // Complete a content-preserving generation switch once the closed generation's stream is
551:   // finished (applied through prior.finalRevision). Content is byte-identical across the
552:   // boundary for every gadget except `discontinuousGadgets`; local buffers carry over -- an
553:   // in-flight submission rides the server's straggler bridge under its old-generation claim,
554:   // and the next submission waits for the pins the bridge derives (see #maybeSubmit). Returns
555:   // "idle" when there is nothing to do (no pending switch, or the old tail is still draining),
556:   // "switched" on success, and "discard" when local edits cannot be carried across (the caller
557:   // discards and rebuilds).
558:   #trySwitchGeneration(): "idle" | "switched" | "discard" {
559:     const target = this.#pendingSwitch
560:     if (target === null) return "idle"
561:     const prior = target.codeBase.prior!
562:     if (this.#appliedRevision < prior.finalRevision) return "idle"  // still draining the tail
563: 
564:     const discontinuous = new Set(prior.discontinuousGadgets)
565: 
566:     // An in-flight submission touching a discontinuous gadget is doomed -- the server rejects
567:     // the whole submission as bridge-ineligible -- and its content basis is gone, so nothing
568:     // local can be preserved either: take the discard path.
569:     if (this.#inflight !== null &&
570:         changedGadgets(this.#inflight.change).some(id => discontinuous.has(id))) {
571:       return "discard"
572:     }
573: 
574:     this.#pendingSwitch = null
575: 
576:     // Drop pending local changes touching discontinuous gadgets (the server would reject them as
577:     // bridge-ineligible; dropping proactively spares the rest of the buffer).
578:     const droppedPending = [...discontinuous].some(id => String(id) in this.#pending)
579:     this.#pending = dropGadgetsFromChange(this.#pending, discontinuous)
580: 
581:     // With nothing in flight, submit the pending buffer *now, under the closing generation's
582:     // claim*, so it rides the server's straggler bridge -- which derives pins from the merge's
583:     // recorded boundary. (A new-generation claim couldn't: the fresh epoch has no pins yet and
584:     // this client cannot know the boundary commits to declare.) Declarations still ride along
585:     // for local-seed gadgets, which were unpinned on both sides of the boundary and follow the
586:     // normal first-touch rule.
587:     if (this.#inflight === null && !isEmptyChange(this.#pending)) {
588:       const pins: ChatGadgetPin[] = changedGadgets(this.#pending)
589:         .filter(gadgetId => !this.#applied.has(gadgetId) && this.#localSeeds.has(gadgetId))
590:         .map(gadgetId =>
591:           ({ gadgetId, baseCommit: this.#localSeeds.get(gadgetId)!.baseCommit }))
592:       const submission: CodeChangeSubmission = {
593:         generation: this.#generation,
594:         revision: this.#appliedRevision,
595:         clientId: this.#clientId,
596:         seq: ++this.#seq,
597:         ...(pins.length > 0 ? { pins } : {}),
598:         change: this.#pending,
599:       }
600:       this.#inflight = { wire: submission, change: this.#pending }
601:       this.#pending = EMPTY_CHANGE
602:       void this.#sendInflight()
603:     }
604: 
605:     // Every pin evaporated: the merged content now lives in commits, and unpinned gadgets track
606:     // head live. Keep entries only for gadgets the local buffers still touch -- for those, the
607:     // old content equals the boundary commit's tree (that is what content-preserving means), so
608:     // local changes keep composing on identical content until the bridged rows re-pin them. Local
609:     // seeds for such gadgets survive too: they were unpinned on both sides, so their base (the
610:     // gadget's untouched head) still stands.
611:     const touched = new Set<WorkpieceId>([
612:       ...changedGadgets(this.#pending),
613:       ...(this.#inflight !== null ? changedGadgets(this.#inflight.change) : []),
614:     ])
615:     const carried: CodeContent = new Map()
616:     for (const gadgetId of touched) {
617:       if (discontinuous.has(gadgetId)) continue
618:       const files = this.#applied.get(gadgetId)
619:       if (files !== undefined) carried.set(gadgetId, files)
620:     }
621:     for (const gadgetId of this.#localSeeds.keys()) {
622:       if (!touched.has(gadgetId)) this.#localSeeds.delete(gadgetId)
623:     }
624:     this.#applied = carried
625:     this.#generation = target.codeBase.generation
626:     this.#appliedRevision = 0
627:     this.#recomputeDisplay()
628:     this.#delegate.onRemoteChange([])
629:     if (droppedPending) this.#delegate.onLocalEditsDiscarded()
630:     this.#scheduleSubmit()
631:     return "switched"
632:   }
633: 
634:   // Discard the local buffers and rebuild from the latest durable snapshot, notifying only if
635:   // keystrokes were actually lost.
636:   async #discardLocalAndRebuild(): Promise<void> {
637:     const hadLocalEdits = this.hasLocalEdits() || this.#localSeeds.size > 0
638:     await this.#rebuild(this.#latestDurable)
639:     if (hadLocalEdits && !this.#fatal) this.#delegate.onLocalEditsDiscarded()
640:   }
641: 
642:   // Rebuild server-acked state from a durable snapshot, dropping local buffers. This is a
643:   // client-session boundary: a fresh clientId, per the submitCodeChange contract.
644:   async #rebuild(durable: ChatDurableCode): Promise<void> {
645:     const codeBase = durable.codeBase ?? { pins: [], generation: 0, revision: 0 }
646: 
647:     // Prefetch every pin's base tree (oid-cached, so repeats are cheap).
648:     const bases = new Map<WorkpieceId, ReadonlyMap<string, string>>()
649:     try {
650:       await Promise.all(codeBase.pins.map(async pin => {
651:         bases.set(pin.gadgetId, await this.#delegate.fetchCommitFiles(pin.baseCommit))
652:       }))

15:   setThemeMode: (mode: ThemeMode) => void
16: }
17: 
18: const ThemeContext = createContext<ThemeContextValue | null>(null)

21:   const themeMode = readThemeMode()
22:   return { themeMode, resolvedThemeMode: resolveThemeMode(themeMode) }
23: }
24: 
25: export function ThemeProvider({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
26:   const [themeState, setThemeState] = useState(getInitialThemeState)
27:   const { themeMode, resolvedThemeMode } = themeState
28: 
29:   useEffect(() => {
30:     if (themeMode !== 'system') {
31:       applyThemeMode(themeMode)
32:       return
33:     }
34: 
35:     const mediaQuery = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')
36:     const handleChange = () => {
37:       const nextResolved = applyThemeMode('system')
38:       setThemeState((prev) => prev.resolvedThemeMode === nextResolved
39:         ? prev
40:         : { ...prev, resolvedThemeMode: nextResolved })
41:     }
42:     mediaQuery.addEventListener('change', handleChange)
43:     return () => mediaQuery.removeEventListener('change', handleChange)
44:   }, [themeMode])
45: 
46:   const value = useMemo<ThemeContextValue>(() => ({
47:     themeMode,
48:     resolvedThemeMode,
49:     setThemeMode: (mode) => {
50:       writeThemeMode(mode)
51:       setThemeState({ themeMode: mode, resolvedThemeMode: applyThemeMode(mode) })
52:     },
53:   }), [themeMode, resolvedThemeMode])
54: 
55:   return <ThemeContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</ThemeContext.Provider>
56: }
57:

/** A specific resource within a connection (channel, doc URL, repo, etc.) */
export interface ConnectionResource {
  id: string
  label: string
  /** e.g. "#general", "https://docs.google.com/...", "org/repo" */
  value: string
  /** Resource type hint */
  type: 'channel' | 'url' | 'repo' | 'project' | 'board' | 'page' | 'file' | 'server' | 'database'
  active: boolean
}

/** Describes what kind of resource input a connection accepts */
export interface ResourceConfig {
  /** What the user adds: channels, URLs, repos, etc. */
  resourceType: 'channel' | 'url' | 'repo' | 'project' | 'board' | 'page' | 'file' | 'server' | 'database'
  /** Placeholder text for the input */
  placeholder: string
  /** Label shown above the input */
  inputLabel: string
  /** Whether the connection offers a browse/search picker (vs. paste-only) */
  browsable: boolean
}

export interface Connection {
  id: string
  name: string
  description: string

  logo: string

  color: string

  bgColor: string
  connected: boolean

  /** Configured resources for this connection */
  resources?: ConnectionResource[]

  resourceConfig?: ResourceConfig

/**
 * Shared CodeMirror theme + monospace font stack used by the code view's editors (CodeEditor
 * and CodeDiffEditor). Ported from the Workshop's former Monaco theme -- the palette is the
 * same one gatekeeper-context's Monaco-matched CodeMirror theme uses, so gadget code looks
 * identical across surfaces. The diff layer's own styling lives in CodeDiffEditor.css.
 */

import { EditorView } from '@codemirror/view'
import { HighlightStyle, syntaxHighlighting } from '@codemirror/language'
import { tags as t } from '@lezer/highlight'
import type { Extension } from '@codemirror/state'
import type { ResolvedThemeMode } from '../theme'

export const monoFont =
  'ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, "Liberation Mono", "Courier New", monospace'

const highlightLight = HighlightStyle.define([
  { tag: t.comment, color: '#a39990', fontStyle: 'italic' },
  {
    tag: [
      t.keyword, t.moduleKeyword, t.controlKeyword, t.operatorKeyword, t.definitionKeyword,
      t.modifier, t.self,
    ],
    color: '#8e3aa6',
  },
  { tag: t.operator, color: '#6b6157' },
  { tag: [t.string, t.special(t.string), t.regexp, t.escape], color: '#4d8a44' },
  { tag: [t.number, t.bool, t.null, t.atom], color: '#b56a1f' },
  { tag: [t.typeName, t.className, t.namespace], color: '#b56a1f' },
  { tag: [t.function(t.variableName), t.function(t.propertyName)], color: '#3a72c9' },
  { tag: [t.variableName, t.propertyName], color: '#1f1d1a' },
  { tag: t.constant(t.variableName), color: '#b56a1f' },
  { tag: t.standard(t.variableName), color: '#3a72c9' },
  { tag: [t.punctuation, t.separator, t.bracket, t.paren, t.brace], color: '#6b6157' },
  { tag: t.tagName, color: '#c14438' },
  { tag: t.attributeName, color: '#b56a1f' },
  { tag: t.attributeValue, color: '#4d8a44' },
  { tag: t.heading, color: '#8e3aa6' },
  { tag: t.url, color: '#4d8a44' },
])

const highlightDark = HighlightStyle.define([
  { tag: t.comment, color: '#858396', fontStyle: 'italic' },
  {
    tag: [
      t.keyword, t.moduleKeyword, t.controlKeyword, t.operatorKeyword, t.definitionKeyword,
      t.modifier, t.self,
    ],
    color: '#d8b4fe',
  },
  { tag: t.operator, color: '#b9b5c8' },
  { tag: [t.string, t.special(t.string), t.regexp, t.escape], color: '#86efac' },
  { tag: [t.number, t.bool, t.null, t.atom], color: '#fbbf24' },
  { tag: [t.typeName, t.className, t.namespace], color: '#fbbf24' },
  { tag: [t.function(t.variableName), t.function(t.propertyName)], color: '#93c5fd' },
  { tag: [t.variableName, t.propertyName], color: '#e8e6f0' },
  { tag: t.constant(t.variableName), color: '#fbbf24' },
  { tag: t.standard(t.variableName), color: '#93c5fd' },
  { tag: [t.punctuation, t.separator, t.bracket, t.paren, t.brace], color: '#b9b5c8' },
  { tag: t.tagName, color: '#fca5a5' },
  { tag: t.attributeName, color: '#fbbf24' },
  { tag: t.attributeValue, color: '#86efac' },
  { tag: t.heading, color: '#d8b4fe' },
  { tag: t.url, color: '#86efac' },
])

// Shared structural rules (fonts, sizing, gutters), parameterized by palette.
function editorChrome(colors: {
  bg: string; fg: string; gutter: string; gutterActive: string; selection: string
  inactiveSelection: string; matchHighlight: string; panelBg: string; line: string
}, dark: boolean): Extension {
  return EditorView.theme(
    {
      '&': {
        color: colors.fg,
        backgroundColor: colors.bg,
        height: '100%',
        fontSize: '13px',
      },
      '&.cm-focused': { outline: 'none' },
      '.cm-scroller': {
        fontFamily: monoFont,
        lineHeight: '20px',
        overflow: 'auto',
      },
      '.cm-content': { padding: '12px 0', caretColor: colors.fg },
      '.cm-line': { padding: '0 16px 0 12px' },
      '.cm-gutters': {
        backgroundColor: colors.bg,
        border: 'none',
        color: colors.gutter,
        fontSize: '12px',
      },
      '.cm-lineNumbers .cm-gutterElement': { padding: '0 8px 0 14px', minWidth: '36px' },
      '.cm-activeLine': { backgroundColor: 'transparent' },
      '.cm-activeLineGutter': { backgroundColor: 'transparent', color: colors.gutterActive },
      '.cm-cursor, .cm-dropCursor': { borderLeftColor: colors.fg },
      '&.cm-focused > .cm-scroller > .cm-selectionLayer .cm-selectionBackground, .cm-content ::selection':
        { backgroundColor: colors.selection },
      '.cm-selectionBackground': { backgroundColor: colors.inactiveSelection },
      '.cm-selectionMatch': { backgroundColor: colors.matchHighlight },
      '.cm-searchMatch': { backgroundColor: colors.matchHighlight },
      '.cm-searchMatch.cm-searchMatch-selected': { backgroundColor: colors.selection },
      '.cm-panels': { backgroundColor: colors.panelBg, color: colors.fg },
      '.cm-panels.cm-panels-bottom': { borderTop: `1px solid ${colors.line}` },
      '.cm-panel.cm-search [name=close]': { color: colors.fg },
      '.cm-foldGutter .cm-gutterElement': { cursor: 'pointer' },
      '.cm-foldPlaceholder': {
        backgroundColor: 'transparent',
        border: 'none',
        color: colors.gutterActive,
      },
    },
    { dark },
  )
}

const chromeLight = editorChrome({
  bg: '#fffdfb',
  fg: '#1f1d1a',
  gutter: '#cabfb2',
  gutterActive: '#796c63',
  selection: '#b3d4ff',
  inactiveSelection: '#dbe6f5',
  matchHighlight: '#cee0fa',
  panelBg: '#faf6f1',
  line: '#efe4d6',
}, false)

const chromeDark = editorChrome({
  bg: '#16151f',
  fg: '#e8e6f0',
  gutter: '#6d6880',
  gutterActive: '#b9b5c8',
  selection: '#4b3d66',
  inactiveSelection: '#352f4a',
  matchHighlight: '#352f4a',
  panelBg: '#1d1c29',
  line: '#2a263b',
}, true)

/** The editor theme (chrome + syntax highlighting) for the given resolved UI theme mode. */
export function codeEditorTheme(mode: ResolvedThemeMode): Extension {
  return mode === 'dark'
    ? [chromeDark, syntaxHighlighting(highlightDark)]
    : [chromeLight, syntaxHighlighting(highlightLight)]
}

21: //
22: // Committed code is git commits; the gadget's head commit (`headCommitId`, from
23: // WorkpieceSummary.commitId) is fetched with Overseer.getCodeAtCommit() -- immutable, so cached
24: // by oid -- and is both the read-only view outside any chat and the "original" side of in-chat
25: // diffs. A chat's uncommitted changes are a revisioned stream of code changes (see ChatCodeBase in
26: // the API), tracked here by a per-chat ChatOtClient (see otClient.ts): the chat's content is
27: // its pins' base trees plus the epoch's recorded changes plus live rows, and the user's edits are
28: // composed locally and submitted through Overseer.submitCodeChange().
29: //
30: // A gadget not pinned in the chat tracks mainline head live. The user can start editing it
31: // without any round trip: the editor shows the head tree, and the first local edit seeds the
32: // client's content from that same tree and declares the pin on its next submission (the
33: // first-keystroke pin flow; see ChatOtClient.ensureGadgetEditable). If the server refuses a
34: // submission -- the chat's generation moved destructively under a revert/draft-discard, or the
35: // pin declaration lost a race -- the queued local edits are discarded with a notice and the
36: // view rebuilds from server state, per ChatCodeBase.generation's contract. Merges don't
37: // discard anything: the client rides the epoch reset (and the server's straggler bridge)
